interpretation: Stations 14, 15 and 16 retain exhaust castings before the intake is present; a model must not depend on intake material for their initial retention.
Stud 13 participates in the front exhaust and lifting-eye installation. The text does not establish the stud thread, nut/washer stack or every contact of the eye.

The image shows upper and lower attachment positions, not sixteen identical bolts at equal spacing. Shared contact at a schematic joint is insufficient evidence for a particular clamp section or washer count.
The lifting-eye outline extends inboard of station 13 above the front intake mouths. A miniature eye placed only around a convenient new stud would not reproduce that traced outline.
The separate single intake locating dowel is not one of these clamping fasteners. Existing upper-intake studs are a different joint.

manufacturer_photo_review.result: 674-185 exterior view supports a three-port front exhaust replacement casting and packaged loose studs/nuts. Head-facing holes, shared clamp sections and lifting-eye stack are not exposed. Package quantity cannot be substituted for head station count.

candidate_constraints: Current exhaust head branches have no mounting lugs; any functional fastener requires explicit casting-interface geometry, head socket, bearing seat and clearance checks.

Current lower-intake continuous upper strip occupies Y -145.5 to -135.5, Z 295.5 to 305.5 across X +/-344. Upper exhaust lugs cannot be added through this strip without a deliberate joint reconciliation.

A provisional station-13 stud beyond the front branch is geometrically conceivable, but its location and the lifting-eye support footprint are not recovered from dimensions. It must not be presented as installed Ford hardware.
No physical clamp candidate is accepted from this source alone; retain missing shared hardware explicitly rather than installing cosmetic floating bolts.
